lines.en: Hi everyone! Welcome to LS2: Free Time, Live! In this short video, you'll see your goals, your final product, and the grammar and words you need.
Our big question is: what do we really do in our free time? We look at hobbies and events, like a match, a concert or a Saturday at the skate park.

slide.text: What do we really do in our free time?

lines.en: You have four goals. One: understand short vlogs, posts and web pages about hobbies. What are people doing now, and what do they usually do?
Two: check if a web page is reliable. Who wrote it? When? Why? Then make a fact file and give credit to your sources.
Three: speak live, like a vlogger. Say what people are doing now, and compare it with what they usually do.
And four: write a vlog script, with tips for a healthy use of screens.
At the end, you make your own Free Time Vlog: a video of one and a half to two minutes about a hobby or an event, with Google Slides and your face in a small window.

slide.title: Your Free Time Vlog
points: Google Slides + your face in a small window

lines.en: It has seven slides: hello, what is happening now, what usually happens, a photo or facts, your likes, your screen tips, and the credits.

You work step by step: choose a hobby or event, check your source, write your script, make your slides, record, improve one part, and submit it on Classroom. A vlog buddy helps you, but every vlog is your own.

slide.note: A vlog buddy helps you, but every vlog is your own.

lines.en: The final product is twenty-five percent of your LS mark. Your vlog counts most. Then your script and slides, your source, your fact file, and your work on every step.

slide.kicker: Final product · 25 % of your LS mark

lines.en: Now, the grammar. The star of this LS is the Present Continuous: am, is or are, plus a verb ending in i-n-g. I'm watching a match. They're playing volleyball. Are you having fun? Yes, I am!

slide.title: Present Continuous: am / is / are + -ing
slide.note: now · right now · at the moment · today

lines.en: Careful with the spelling: dance, dancing. Swim, swimming. Play, playing.

Compare it with the Present Simple: the Present Simple for what you usually do, the Present Continuous for now. I usually play football on Saturdays, but today I'm watching a match. And some verbs, like like and know, never take i-n-g. Say: I like it.

slide.title: Usually or now?
slide.note: Some verbs don't take -ing: I like it. (not I'm liking it) · know · want · prefer

lines.en: For likes, use love, like, don't like or hate, plus i-n-g: I love skating. And for screen tips, use imperatives: Take a break. Don't use your phone in bed.

slide.title: Likes + -ing · Tips with imperatives
examples: I love skating. I hate getting up early.

lines.en: And the words you need: free-time activities, like go swimming or do karate. Clothes and kit, like trainers or a helmet. The weather. Events, like a match or a festival. Time words, like now and at the moment. And screen words, like screen time.

groups: play basketball · go swimming · do karate
It's sunny · It's raining · It's windy
a concert · a match · a festival
now · at the moment · on Saturdays
upload a video · screen time · take a break

lines.en: Do the learning paths in order. Each one gives you a piece of your vlog, so at the end your vlog is easy to make. Have fun, and let's go live!

slide.title: Let's go live!
